memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said to him, 'In my dream I saw a vine in front of me, and on the vine were three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters ripened into grapes. Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup and put the cup in his hand.'" - Gen 40:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chief cupbearer opens up and tells Joseph his dream in detail — a vine with three branches, budding and blossoming, ripening into grapes, and his own hands pressing them into Pharaoh's cup. And Joseph listens. Before he speaks a word of interpretation, he gives the man his full attention, letting him pour out every detail.

There is a simple but important lesson in this listening. Joseph did not rush to give an answer or cut the man off. He created space for the cupbearer to be heard. So often, the first gift we can give a troubled person is not our advice but our attention — a willingness to truly listen.

The dream itself is full of hope, though the cupbearer does not yet know it. The vine flourishing, the cup returning to Pharaoh's hand — these were signs of restoration to come. But that meaning could only be unfolded once the man had been given the chance to share.

We live in a hurried world, quick to speak and slow to listen. Scripture calls us to the opposite: to be "quick to listen, slow to speak" (Jas 1:19). When someone is carrying something heavy, resist the urge to jump in with solutions. First, listen well. Give people the dignity of your full attention, as Joseph did, and you may find you are able to help them far more.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I quick to listen, or quick to speak?
2. Do I give people my full attention when they share?
3. Whom do I need to listen to more patiently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me quick to listen and slow to speak. Help me to give others the gift of my full attention, and to truly hear people before I rush to respond. Amen.
